title: AP Biology · End-of-course exam — original full-length mock (May 2027)
subject: ap-biology

phases.label: Section I — 60 multiple-choice questions
phases.instructions: Complete all 60 questions. You cannot return after this section ends.

phases.label: Monitored break
phases.instructions: Examination content and responses are locked. Section II opens automatically when this fixed break ends.

phases.label: Section II — 6 free-response questions
phases.instructions: Answer all six questions. Questions 1–2 carry 9 points each; questions 3–6 carry 4 points each. Show reasoning and calculations.

instructions: Original full-length practice for the May 2027 format, not an official or endorsed AP exam. Section I: 60 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes. After a 10-minute monitored break, Section II: two 9-point and four 4-point free-response questions in 90 minutes. Answer every question; choose the best answer for each MCQ. There is no separate reading period. A supplied four-function calculator with square root or scientific nongraphing calculator is permitted in both sections; handheld graphing calculators and handheld calculators with storage capabilities are not permitted under the 2027 policy. Reference facts are attached to every question. Real Bluebook offers Desmos scientific; this practice uses your supplied device. Work free responses in the integrated canvas, adding pages as needed. Explain biological mechanisms and show calculations; label graph axes and units. Real AP uses handwritten response booklets. DigitalDP starts the next section automatically after its fixed break and does not allow a return to an expired section. Raw marks are not an AP scaled score.

resources.label: Biology reference facts · available throughout
resources.text:
Mathematical reference facts, independently typeset for this original practice exam. These are not a reproduction of the College Board reference booklet.
Mean x̄ = Σx/n. Sample standard deviation s = √[Σ(x−x̄)²/(n−1)]. Standard error SE = s/√n. An approximate 95% confidence interval is x̄±2 SE when the sampling assumptions are appropriate; overlap alone is not a formal significance test.
Percent change =100(new−original)/original. Rate = change/time.
χ² = Σ[(observed−expected)²/expected]. For an unadjusted goodness-of-fit test, degrees of freedom = number of categories−1. At p=0.05, critical values: df 1: 3.841; df 2: 5.991; df 3: 7.815. If χ² exceeds the relevant critical value, reject the specified null model at that level.
For a two-allele locus: p+q=1. Hardy–Weinberg expected genotype frequencies: p², 2pq, q². Assumptions: large population, random mating, no mutation, no migration and no selection at the locus.
Independent-event probability: P(A and B)=P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive alternatives: P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B).
Water potential: Ψ=Ψp+Ψs. Solute potential: Ψs=−iCRT, with i the dissociation factor, C in mol L⁻¹, R=0.0831 L bar mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, T in kelvin. Celsius to kelvin: add 273.15.
Exponential growth: dN/dt=rN. Logistic growth: dN/dt=rN(1−N/K), with N population size, r intrinsic per-capita rate, K carrying capacity.
Net primary productivity = gross primary productivity−producer respiration.
Sphere: surface area 4πr², volume 4πr³/3. Rectangular solid: volume lwh, surface area 2(lw+lh+wh).

resources.label: Questions 7–10 · membrane transport study
resources.text:
Original experiment. Researchers placed equal-sized plant tissue cylinders in sucrose solutions for 60 minutes at 25°C. Six independently sampled cylinders were used at each concentration. Cylinders were blotted by the same procedure before weighing. Sucrose did not cross the plasma membranes during the trial.
Sucrose / mol L⁻¹ | Mean mass change / % | Standard error / percentage points
0.00 | +12.0 | 0.8
0.20 | +5.0 | 0.6
0.40 | −3.0 | 0.5
0.60 | −10.0 | 0.9
Assume a straight-line relationship between the two measurements nearest zero mass change when estimating the isotonic concentration.

resources.label: Questions 14–17 · isolated mitochondria
resources.text:
Original experiment. Equal amounts of isolated mitochondria were supplied with excess oxygen, respiratory substrate, ADP and phosphate. The table gives steady rates after treatment, relative to untreated mitochondria. U is a compound that allows protons to move across the inner membrane without passing through ATP synthase. B blocks electron transfer to oxygen. The preparations remained intact.
Treatment | Oxygen consumption | ATP production
None | 100 | 100
U | 155 | 12
B | 4 | 3
Rates are relative units. No claim about statistical significance is possible from these means alone.

resources.label: Questions 22–25 · signaling pathway model
resources.text:
Original model. An extracellular ligand binds receptor R. Activated R activates kinase K. K phosphorylates transcription factor T; phosphorylated T stimulates gene G. An enzyme P removes the phosphate from T. Arrows in the first line show activation. The second line shows the separate dephosphorylation reaction catalyzed by P.
Ligand → R → K → T-P → transcription of G
P catalyzes: T-P → T + phosphate
Without ligand, R is inactive. All proposed mutations affect only the activity named; assume no other pathway regulates G.

resources.label: Questions 30–33 · two-gene test cross
resources.text:
Original genetics study. A plant heterozygous at two linked loci has alleles arranged AB/ab. It is test-crossed with ab/ab. All four offspring phenotypes are equally viable and distinguishable. Offspring counts:
AB phenotype: 410
ab phenotype: 390
Ab phenotype: 102
aB phenotype: 98
Total: 1000
The phenotype records the gamete from the heterozygous parent. Assume the sample estimates the recombination frequency adequately.

resources.label: Questions 36–39 · gene regulation experiment
resources.text:
Original experiment. Researchers introduced a reporter gene into cultured animal cells. The reporter's coding sequence and promoter were identical in all constructs. Constructs differed only in a distant regulatory DNA region. All cells received equal DNA amounts and a second constitutively expressed control reporter. Values below are reporter expression divided by control-reporter expression, averaged over six independent cultures.
Construct | No hormone | Hormone added
Intact regulatory region | 2 | 20
Regulatory region deleted | 2 | 3
Intact region, receptor gene disrupted in cells | 2 | 2
The hormone enters the cells and binds an intracellular receptor.

resources.label: Questions 44–47 · evolutionary evidence
resources.text:
Original simplified rooted tree. O is an outgroup. All terminal labels represent living populations. The topology, not the spacing, is the information supplied.
root
├─ O
└─ node 1
   ├─ A
   └─ node 2
      ├─ B
      └─ node 3
         ├─ C
         └─ D
Independent DNA data: a derived 12-base insertion is absent in O and A but present at the same homologous site in B, C and D. Assume the insertion arose once and was not lost.

resources.label: Questions 54–57 · pond manipulation
resources.text:
Original study. Twenty comparable outdoor pond tanks were randomly assigned to fish-present or fish-absent treatments (10 each). Initial algal and zooplankton populations were similar. Fish eat large zooplankton; large zooplankton graze algae. After four weeks:
Treatment | Mean large zooplankton / L | Mean chlorophyll a / µg L⁻¹
Fish absent | 48 | 6
Fish present | 12 | 24
Light and nutrient supply were held constant. Chlorophyll a is used as a measure of algal abundance. No toxin effect was studied.

resources.label: FRQ 1 · bacterial gene regulation
resources.text:
Original investigation. A bacterium can use sugar S when it produces transporter X. A regulatory protein Q binds a DNA site near the promoter of gene X. Binding inhibits transcription. A small molecule derived from S binds Q and prevents Q from binding DNA. Researchers investigate whether Q and the DNA site regulate gene X as proposed.
All cultures begin with the same cell density and an equal, nonlimiting alternative carbon source. Relative X mRNA is measured after 20 minutes. Growth is measured over the next 6 hours. Means are from 8 independent cultures; values are mean ±2 SE.
Strain | Sugar S | Relative X mRNA | Growth / generations per hour
Wild type | absent | 2±0.4 | 0.30±0.02
Wild type | present | 18±1.2 | 0.62±0.04
Q gene deleted | absent | 19±1.0 | 0.27±0.02
Q gene deleted | present | 20±1.1 | 0.60±0.03
DNA binding site altered | absent | 17±1.0 | 0.28±0.02
DNA binding site altered | present | 18±1.3 | 0.61±0.03
The DNA-site alteration does not change the promoter sequence or the X coding sequence. These are designed teaching data, not results from a published study.

resources.label: FRQ 2 · temperature and respiration
resources.text:
Original investigation. Researchers acclimate equal-mass groups of a small freshwater crustacean to different temperatures for 24 hours. Eight independent chambers per temperature contain equal numbers of organisms in the same volume of oxygenated water. Sensors measure the initial oxygen-consumption rate; no chamber becomes oxygen limited. Matched chambers without organisms measure background oxygen change, which is subtracted. Salinity, food history and light are held constant.
Temperature / °C | Mean oxygen consumption / µmol O₂ g⁻¹ h⁻¹ | 2 SE
10 | 3.2 | 0.4
15 | 4.6 | 0.4
20 | 6.8 | 0.6
25 | 9.2 | 0.8
30 | 6.0 | 0.6
All organisms survive the initial measurement. This study does not directly measure protein shape or enzyme activity.

resources.label: FRQ 3 · seed germination proposal
resources.text: Original scenario. A plant establishes mainly in recently opened canopy gaps. A researcher hypothesizes that light reaching the soil stimulates its seed germination. Seeds can be obtained from many parent plants. The available growth cabinets allow light exposure and temperature to be controlled independently. Germination is defined as emergence of the root from the seed coat.

resources.label: FRQ 4 · chromosome separation
resources.text: Original scenario. An organism has 2n=6. During meiosis I in one precursor cell, the homologous chromosomes of one pair fail to separate and both move to the same pole. The other two pairs separate normally. Meiosis II proceeds normally, and all four products survive. Count each chromosome by its centromere.

resources.label: FRQ 5 · food-web model
resources.text:
Original simplified food web. Each arrow points from a food resource to the consumer receiving matter and energy. These are the only feeding links included in the model.
Grass ──→ rabbit ──→ fox
  │                   ↑
  └──→ grasshopper → frog

Both rabbit and frog are eaten by fox. Grass is a producer. Decomposers are omitted. The model shows feeding relationships, not population sizes, transfer efficiencies or strengths of interactions.

resources.label: FRQ 6 · color composition of survivors
resources.text: Original investigation. A very large, isolated beetle population has known initial proportions of 50% light and 50% dark individuals. It occupies dark substrate with visually hunting predators. After a fixed interval, a researcher takes a simple random sample of 100 survivors: 32 are light and 68 are dark. The sample is a negligible fraction of the remaining population. There is no reproduction or migration during the interval, and individual beetles do not change color. The null hypothesis is that the survivor population still has the initial 50:50 color composition, giving expected sample counts of 50 light and 50 dark. Use a chi-square goodness-of-fit test with 1 degree of freedom and critical value 3.841 at p=0.05. Color has a heritable component, but no offspring are measured here. The numbers initially present and the total numbers surviving are not given.

questions.label: Section I — Question 1
questions.prompt: A pond freezes at its surface while liquid water remains below. Which molecular property most directly explains why the ice floats?
options: Covalent bonds between water molecules become shorter on freezing.
Water molecules lose oxygen atoms as ice forms.
The nonpolar parts of water molecules repel one another.
Hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open arrangement in ice.

questions.label: Section I — Question 2
questions.prompt: In a soluble enzyme, a mutation replaces an uncharged amino acid buried in its hydrophobic core with a charged amino acid. Which outcome is most directly plausible?
options: Altered interactions change folding and possibly the active site.
Every peptide bond in the protein is hydrolyzed.
The genetic code gains a new codon.
The amino-acid sequence becomes a carbohydrate.

questions.label: Section I — Question 3
questions.prompt: A student hydrolyzes a purified polymer and detects only glucose monomers. Which additional observation would best distinguish cellulose from starch?
options: Whether the material contains hydrogen
Whether carbon is present
Whether hydrolysis consumed water
The type of glycosidic linkage joining adjacent glucose units

questions.label: Section I — Question 4
questions.prompt: A membrane lipid contains a phosphate-bearing polar head and two nonpolar fatty-acid tails. In water, which arrangement best reduces exposure of the tails to water?
options: All heads and tails mixed uniformly throughout the water
Heads in the bilayer interior and tails on both outer surfaces
A bilayer with heads facing water and tails facing inward
A covalent chain connecting every head to every tail

questions.label: Section I — Question 5
questions.prompt: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 24% adenine. What percentage of its nucleotides contain cytosine?

questions.label: Section I — Question 6
questions.prompt: A cell links 50 amino acids into one unbranched polypeptide. Ignoring later processing, how many peptide bonds are formed?

questions.label: Section I — Question 7
questions.prompt: Using the specified interpolation, the sucrose concentration producing no net mass change is closest to
options: 0.325 mol L⁻¹
0.500 mol L⁻¹
0.250 mol L⁻¹
0.125 mol L⁻¹

questions.label: Section I — Question 8
questions.prompt: Why did the cylinders in 0.60 mol L⁻¹ sucrose lose mass?
options: Water moved out toward the lower external water potential.
The solution had a higher water potential than the cells.
Sucrose converted intracellular water into ATP.
Active transport pumped all water out of the cells.

questions.label: Section I — Question 9
questions.prompt: Why is standardized blotting important?
options: It limits variation in surface liquid included in measured mass.
It prevents sucrose from dissolving.
It ensures that osmosis proceeds only inward.
It makes every cylinder genetically identical.

questions.label: Section I — Question 10
questions.prompt: A treatment blocks aquaporins without changing solute concentration or killing cells. What is the best prediction for the first few minutes?
options: Water will move against its potential gradient.
Water movement will be slower, but its favored direction is unchanged.
Sucrose will immediately become permeable to the membrane.
The bilayer will necessarily disappear.

questions.label: Section I — Question 11
questions.prompt: Two spherical cells have radii r and 2r. Compared with the smaller cell, the larger cell's surface-area-to-volume ratio is
options: four times as large
half as large
unchanged
twice as large

questions.label: Section I — Question 12
questions.prompt: A cell produces a protein that will be secreted. Which path correctly places major processing and transport steps in order?
options: Plasma membrane → ribosome → chloroplast → Golgi apparatus
Mitochondrion → smooth endoplasmic reticulum → nucleus
Golgi apparatus → nucleus → lysosome → cytosol
Rough endoplasmic reticulum → Golgi apparatus → secretory vesicle → plasma membrane

questions.label: Section I — Question 13
questions.prompt: Which combination most strongly supports an endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria?
options: They contain nuclear chromosomes and are made anew by the Golgi.
They occur only in large organisms and contain cellulose.
They contain circular DNA, divide, and have ribosomes resembling bacterial ribosomes.
They have no membranes and cannot divide.

questions.label: Section I — Question 14
questions.prompt: The data for U most directly support which conclusion?
options: Oxygen consumption alone guarantees a high ATP yield.
ATP synthesis uses no membrane proteins.
A proton gradient is needed to couple electron transport to efficient ATP synthesis.
Electron transfer ceases whenever protons cross the inner membrane.

questions.label: Section I — Question 15
questions.prompt: In untreated mitochondria, oxygen directly participates as
options: the carbon source for acetyl-CoA
the phosphate donor to ADP
the terminal electron acceptor, forming water
the enzyme that splits glucose

questions.label: Section I — Question 16
questions.prompt: What is the percentage decrease in ATP-production rate under U relative to the untreated preparation?

questions.label: Section I — Question 17
questions.prompt: Immediately after B is added, before respiratory substrate is exhausted, which change is expected?
options: ATP synthase begins creating oxygen from carbon dioxide.
Upstream electron carriers become more reduced.
All NADH is instantly oxidized to NAD⁺.
The oxygen-consumption rate rises above that under U.

questions.label: Section I — Question 18
questions.prompt: At fixed enzyme concentration, doubling a very high substrate concentration causes almost no further increase in reaction rate. Which explanation best fits?
options: Activation energy has become negative.
The substrate has become an enzyme.
Most active sites are already occupied; enzyme turnover limits the rate.
The enzyme changed the equilibrium constant.

questions.label: Section I — Question 19
questions.prompt: A leaf is supplied with water containing the isotope oxygen-18 while its carbon dioxide contains ordinary oxygen. During photosynthesis, oxygen-18 will most directly appear in
options: new nitrogen bases
the magnesium in chlorophyll
the carbon atoms of glucose
the oxygen gas released by the light reactions

questions.label: Section I — Question 20
questions.prompt: If light reactions stop but the Calvin cycle briefly continues, which stored molecules will be consumed directly to reduce carbon intermediates and regenerate the CO₂ acceptor?
options: Oxygen and DNA
Carbon dioxide and ADP as energy donors
ATP and NADPH
NADH and glycogen only

questions.label: Section I — Question 21
questions.prompt: Yeast cells produce ethanol when oxygen is absent. How does fermentation allow glycolysis to continue?
options: It replaces all enzymes in glycolysis.
It converts every glucose directly into 36 ATP.
It creates an inner-membrane proton gradient using oxygen.
It regenerates NAD⁺ by oxidizing NADH.

questions.label: Section I — Question 22
questions.prompt: A mutation makes K active even when R is inactive. Which result is predicted without ligand?
options: Transcription of G can occur downstream of constitutively active K.
T can no longer contain amino acids.
P must become a receptor.
G cannot be transcribed because ligand is the RNA template.

questions.label: Section I — Question 23
questions.prompt: If P is inhibited after ligand is removed, which change is most likely?
options: T-P disappears more rapidly.
T remains phosphorylated for longer.
The promoter of G is deleted.
Ligand is converted into DNA.

questions.label: Section I — Question 24
questions.prompt: Which measurement most directly tests whether a drug inhibits the step between K and T?
options: Total water mass in the culture dish
Ligand color after heating it alone
The number of chromosomes in an unrelated organism
T phosphorylation with purified active K, with and without the drug

questions.label: Section I — Question 25
questions.prompt: R still binds ligand, but a deletion removes its domain that activates K. What is expected?
options: Ligand binding no longer efficiently activates this pathway.
G is always maximally expressed.
P becomes unable to remove phosphate.
The ligand automatically phosphorylates T.

questions.label: Section I — Question 26
questions.prompt: Blood glucose rises after a meal, stimulating insulin secretion. Insulin increases glucose uptake, and insulin secretion falls as glucose returns toward its usual range. This is negative feedback because
options: the response amplifies the original rise without limit
all communication occurs by direct DNA transfer
the response permanently eliminates glucose
the response reduces the stimulus that initiated it

questions.label: Section I — Question 27
questions.prompt: A drug prevents spindle microtubules from attaching correctly to kinetochores. Which checkpoint most directly prevents chromosome separation in affected cells?
options: The checkpoint controlling fertilization
The checkpoint determining whether nutrients enter a lysosome
The spindle-assembly checkpoint before anaphase
The checkpoint that removes introns

questions.label: Section I — Question 28
questions.prompt: A tumor-suppressor protein normally halts division when DNA damage is detected. A cell loses both functional copies of its gene. Which consequence is most plausible?
options: The mutation guarantees beneficial changes in offspring.
Every mutation is immediately repaired.
The cell may divide despite unrepaired DNA damage.
The cell necessarily loses all ribosomes.

questions.label: Section I — Question 29
questions.prompt: In a dividing cell culture, most cells have either 2C or 4C DNA, and a smaller group have values between 2C and 4C. The intermediate group most likely consists of cells
options: in G₁ before DNA replication
in S phase synthesizing DNA
that have finished mitosis and cytokinesis
undergoing meiosis II after chromosome separation

questions.label: Section I — Question 30
questions.prompt: The estimated recombination frequency between the loci is

questions.label: Section I — Question 31
questions.prompt: Which event can directly generate the Ab and aB gametes from this heterozygote?
options: DNA replication after fertilization
Exchange between nonsister chromatids of homologous chromosomes in prophase I
Conversion of every recessive allele into a dominant allele
Separation of sister chromatids without any earlier crossing over

questions.label: Section I — Question 32
questions.prompt: Why is the ab/ab parent useful in this cross?
options: It prevents meiosis in the heterozygote.
It guarantees all offspring are homozygous dominant.
Its gametes contribute only a and b, allowing offspring phenotype to reveal the other parent's gamete.
It forces the two genes to become unlinked.

questions.label: Section I — Question 33
questions.prompt: If a second pair of loci independently assort, which offspring ratio is expected in an equivalent two-gene test cross with complete dominance?

questions.label: Section I — Question 34
questions.prompt: Two unaffected parents have an affected daughter for a rare fully penetrant recessive trait. Assume no new mutation. Which inheritance pattern is consistent with this observation?
options: X-linked recessive with an unaffected father
Mitochondrial inheritance with an unaffected homoplasmic mother
Autosomal recessive with both parents heterozygous
Y-linked inheritance

questions.label: Section I — Question 35
questions.prompt: For the cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance and independent offspring outcomes, what is the probability that the first two offspring both have the recessive phenotype?

questions.label: Section I — Question 36
questions.prompt: Which interpretation best fits the regulatory-region deletion?
options: The region contributes to hormone-dependent enhancement of transcription.
The hormone always destroys reporter mRNA.
Deleting the region eliminates every promoter in the cell.
The region is the only template for the reporter's amino acids.

questions.label: Section I — Question 37
questions.prompt: For the intact construct, hormone produces what fold-change relative to no hormone?
options: 10-fold
2-fold
20-fold
18-fold

questions.label: Section I — Question 38
questions.prompt: Why divide reporter expression by the control-reporter expression?
options: To ensure the experimental reporter is never transcribed
To make all regulatory sequences identical
To help control for variation in DNA delivery and cell amount
To convert the hormone into an enzyme

questions.label: Section I — Question 39
questions.prompt: Which extra experiment would best test whether the receptor directly binds the regulatory DNA?
options: Measure the mass of hormone before adding cells.
Measure binding between purified receptor and isolated regulatory DNA, with nonspecific DNA and no-receptor controls.
Delete all ribosomes and measure cell survival.
Count cells without examining DNA.

questions.label: Section I — Question 40
questions.prompt: Why is one new DNA strand synthesized in short fragments at a replication fork?
options: The two parental strands have the same direction.
DNA polymerase adds nucleotides only to a 3′ end, while the templates are antiparallel.
DNA polymerase can synthesize only RNA.
Hydrogen bonds can form only every 100 nucleotides.

questions.label: Section I — Question 41
questions.prompt: Within a protein-coding sequence, one nucleotide is deleted near the start and no compensating insertion occurs. Which result is most likely?
options: Transcription becomes impossible in every cell.
Only the last amino acid is necessarily affected.
Every codon after the deletion is necessarily synonymous.
The reading frame shifts downstream, often producing an early stop codon.

questions.label: Section I — Question 42
questions.prompt: Two cell types have the same gene but produce proteins differing by an internal amino-acid segment. Their mature mRNAs differ by one exon. Which mechanism best explains this?
options: Independent assortment of chromosomes in every transcription event
Replacement of ribosomes by DNA polymerase
Alternative splicing of the same primary RNA transcript
Hydrolysis of all peptide bonds after translation

questions.label: Section I — Question 43
questions.prompt: A PCR tube contains template DNA, thermostable polymerase, nucleotides and buffer but lacks primers. Why will efficient amplification fail?
options: Primers supply all of the template's carbon atoms.
Polymerase needs a paired primer with a free 3′ end to extend.
DNA must be translated before it can be copied.
Thermostable polymerase functions only at 0°C.

questions.label: Section I — Question 44
questions.prompt: Which pair shares the most recent common ancestor in the tree?
options: B and D
O and A
A and B
C and D

questions.label: Section I — Question 45
questions.prompt: On the stated single-origin assumption, the insertion most likely arose on the branch leading to
options: O only
node 2, the ancestor of B, C and D
the common ancestor of all five groups
A only

questions.label: Section I — Question 46
questions.prompt: Which statement is justified by the topology alone?
options: Every branch represents exactly 1 million years.
A has evolved less than D.
B is equally related to C and D through their shared ancestor at node 2.
Living C is the direct ancestor of living D.

questions.label: Section I — Question 47
questions.prompt: Why is a matching insertion at a homologous site stronger evidence of shared ancestry than similar body shape alone?
options: All DNA sequences mutate at the same rate.
Similar shape may arise independently under similar selection pressures.
DNA insertions are unaffected by evolution.
Body shape can never be inherited.

questions.label: Section I — Question 48
questions.prompt: In a large population at Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 9% of individuals are aa. What fraction is expected to be Aa?

questions.label: Section I — Question 49
questions.prompt: A storm leaves only 12 randomly surviving individuals from a large beetle population. A rare neutral allele becomes common among their descendants. Which process best explains the initial change?
options: Artificial selection by humans
Directed mutation because the beetles needed the allele
Independent assortment eliminating every allele
Genetic drift following a population bottleneck

questions.label: Section I — Question 50
questions.prompt: Before an antibiotic is used, a few bacteria already carry a resistance allele. During treatment they leave more descendants than susceptible bacteria. Which explanation is best?
options: Resistance proves that mutation is always beneficial.
The antibiotic instructed all cells to make the same useful mutation.
Selection increased the frequency of pre-existing heritable variation.
Individual susceptible cells evolved by deciding to survive.

questions.label: Section I — Question 51
questions.prompt: Two frog populations live in the same wetland but breed in different months. Even when they meet, few pairs form. The different breeding season is primarily
options: a mechanism requiring different chromosome numbers
a postzygotic barrier caused by hybrid sterility
a prezygotic temporal barrier reducing gene flow
evidence that the populations have identical gene pools

questions.label: Section I — Question 52
questions.prompt: At a locus, AA individuals leave an average of 4 surviving offspring, Aa leave 5, and aa leave 2 under the same conditions. If these differences persist, which outcome is most plausible?
options: Both alleles can be maintained by heterozygote advantage.
The A allele is necessarily neutral.
The a allele must disappear immediately.
The population must stop reproducing.

questions.label: Section I — Question 53
questions.prompt: A laboratory RNA molecule both stores a sequence and catalyzes a reaction. Why is this relevant to hypotheses about early life?
options: It proves the exact location where life began.
It shows that one molecular class can have informational and catalytic roles.
It demonstrates that RNA contains no genetic information.
It shows that all modern proteins are unnecessary.

questions.label: Section I — Question 54
questions.prompt: Which mechanism best accounts for the higher chlorophyll concentration when fish are present?
options: Fish necessarily add a toxin that kills algae.
Fish produce all of the algae by mitosis.
Algae eat the fish and acquire their chlorophyll.
Fish reduce grazers, indirectly releasing algae from grazing pressure.

questions.label: Section I — Question 55
questions.prompt: What is the independent experimental unit?
options: Each molecule of chlorophyll
Each pond tank
Each fish gill
Each reading from one water sample

questions.label: Section I — Question 56
questions.prompt: Relative to fish-absent tanks, the mean zooplankton abundance in fish-present tanks decreased by

questions.label: Section I — Question 57
questions.prompt: Which conclusion goes beyond the evidence?
options: Fish treatment is associated with lower mean zooplankton abundance.
The manipulated food web can show indirect effects.
Adding fish will improve biodiversity in every natural pond.
The experiment tests a specific fish–grazer–algae interaction.

questions.label: Section I — Question 58
questions.prompt: A population follows dN/dt=rN(1−N/K), with r=0.20 year⁻¹, K=1000 and N=500. What is its predicted instantaneous growth rate?
options: 100 individuals year⁻¹
200 individuals year⁻¹
20 individuals year⁻¹
50 individuals year⁻¹

questions.label: Section I — Question 59
questions.prompt: A grassland has gross primary productivity of 1800 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and producer respiration of 700 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Its net primary productivity is
options: 1100 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹
2500 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹
700 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹
1800 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹

questions.label: Section I — Question 60
questions.prompt: Two communities each contain four species and 100 individuals. Community X has 25 of each species; community Y has 97 of one species and 1 of each other species. Which comparison is correct?
options: Y has greater richness because one species is abundant.
Evenness must be equal because total abundance is equal.
X has fewer species than Y.
Richness is equal, but X has greater evenness.

questions.label: Section II — Question 1
questions.prompt:
(a) Describe the role of a promoter in transcription. [1]
(b)(i) Identify the dependent variable that directly measures gene X transcriptional output. [1]
(ii) Explain why the wild-type strain grown without S is an appropriate comparison for wild type grown with S. [1]
(c)(i) Calculate the fold-change in mean X mRNA when S is added to wild type. Show your calculation. [1]
(ii) Use one comparison involving the Q-deletion strain and one involving the altered DNA site to explain how the data support the proposed regulatory model. [2]
(d)(i) A new Q allele produces a protein that binds the DNA site normally but cannot bind the S-derived molecule. Predict X mRNA in this strain when S is present relative to wild type with S, and justify your prediction. [2]
(ii) Explain one possible resource-allocation reason why constitutive X production could reduce growth when S is absent. [1]

questions.label: Section II — Question 2
questions.prompt:
(a) Explain why oxygen consumption can provide evidence about the rate of aerobic respiration. [1]
(b) Construct a graph of the data, including appropriately scaled and labeled axes, all means, and ±2 SE error bars. [3]
(c)(i) Describe the pattern across 10–30°C, including the temperature with the highest measured mean. [1]
(ii) Calculate the percentage increase in mean rate from 10°C to 25°C. Show your work. [1]
(d)(i) Predict how the rate at 20°C would change if an inhibitor blocked transfer of electrons to oxygen, and explain the cellular basis of the prediction. [2]
(ii) A student claims that the fall at 30°C proves respiratory enzymes denatured. Explain why the measurements do not establish that mechanism. [1]

questions.label: Section II — Question 3
questions.prompt:
